comp_disc_analysis.notes:
[chunk 1/2] This DEF 14A Compensation Discussion & Analysis section is almost entirely boilerplate executive compensation governance, salary tables, RSU vesting schedules, and peer group benchmarking. No SIFI-material entities were identified: no SPVs, off-balance-sheet entities, AI lab investments, capex commitments, circularity arrangements, revenue roundtripping, or customer/supplier concentration disclosures appear in this section. The peer group listing (Alphabet, Amazon, Apple, AT&T, Cisco, Comcast, Microsoft, Netflix, PayPal, Salesforce, Disney, Uber, Verizon, and for 2025: NVIDIA, Oracle, Visa added) is noted for completeness but represents standard compensation benchmarking practice with no counterparty-web implications. NVIDIA's addition to Meta's 2025 peer group is noted as a weak signal of Meta's self-positioning relative to large-cap AI/infrastructure peers, but does not constitute a material relationship disclosure. No edges are emitted as there are no disclosed business relationships, investments, or risk signals in this section that meet the SIFI-materiality threshold.
[chunk 2/2] This DEF 14A Compensation Discussion & Analysis section is largely boilerplate executive compensation disclosure with minimal SIFI-material content. Two signals extracted: (1) Zuckerberg's share pledge (12M Class B shares, ~2.1% voting power) creates a hidden leverage / forced-sale risk at the controlling-shareholder level — severity kept at 2 because the pledge is capped at 20% of holdings and loan LTV at 5% FMV per disclosed framework. (2) Meta's payment for Zuckerberg's personal use of an aircraft he indirectly owns is a related-party arrangement disclosed under "Related Party Transactions" per the filing — extracted as OTHER/severity 1 for counterparty-web completeness. No AI lab investments, SPVs, capex commitments, or supplier/customer concentration data appear in this section. Routine RSU grants, say-on-pay disclosures, Section 162(m) discussion, and CEO pay ratio are not SIFI-material and were skipped.

director_comp.notes:
[chunk 1/4] FILING: Meta DEF 14A (2025-04-17). SECTION: Director Compensation and Security Ownership. SIFI EXTRACTION: This section contains minimal SIFI-material content. The director compensation disclosures are standard governance-level details with no hidden leverage, related-party circularity, or counterparty concentration risk beyond routine public disclosure. Key findings: (1) Mark Zuckerberg retains 99.8% voting control via Class B shares (342.6M shares, 10 votes/share) while holding only 14% economic interest—severe voting-economic divergence. (2) Three passive institutional investors (BlackRock 7.2%, Vanguard 8.5%, Fidelity 6.1% of Class A) collectively hold 22% of economic equity but zero voting power due to dual-class structure. (3) Director personal security costs ($833K+ for Ms. Alford in 2024) are expensed without compensation cap adjustment, creating potential governance optics risk but no SIFI leverage or counterparty risk. (4) Deferred Compensation Plan enables RSU deferral for directors Arnold and Kimmitt, but amounts are immaterial to systemic risk. (5) Related-party identification: CZI Holdings LLC, Chan Zuckerberg Holdings LLC/II/III, Mark Zuckerberg Trust—all Zuckerberg control vehicles, no external counterparty exposure. (6) Shareholder proposal (Proposal Six) explicitly notes the governance tension: 84% shareholder support for recapitalization to one-share-one-vote, but board defends dual-class structure as enabling long-term focus. This is a governance/agency risk, not a SIFI financial risk. EXCLUDED: Standard director RSU vesting schedules, annual retainer tables, excess meeting fees, stock ownership guidelines—all boilerplate. CONCLUSION: No extraction of hidden_risk_signal or capex_commitment nodes warranted. The section documents passive index fund holdings and routine governance, not SIFI material."
